workingTitle: Warped galaxies place a tight limit on a dark fifth force
topic: Gravity & Fundamental Physics / Cosmology & Early Universe
publicationStatus: Preliminary preprint; not yet peer reviewed; authors state it is to be submitted to Physical Review D.
coreFacts: The authors measured U-shaped warp statistics for 3,968 usable edge-on disk galaxies drawn from Sloan Digital Sky Survey imaging.
A fifth force acting on dark matter but not stars would offset each galaxy's halo from its stellar disk and predict a cup-shaped warp aligned with the surrounding dark-matter field.
The measured warps show no statistically supported correlation with that predicted fifth-force field.
For force ranges of 8 megaparsecs and above, the fiducial 95% upper limit is 7.7e-4 of Newtonian gravity; an envelope over tested systematic variations gives a conservative limit of 1.7e-3.
For an effectively infinite-range rolling scalar, the authors report that the conservative limit is about three times tighter than the cited cosmological bound.
caveats: The work is a new, unreviewed preprint.
The conservative limit is an envelope across model variations, not a standard single-model credible interval.
Galaxy halo profiles, baryonic warps, idealised disk structure, dust, and correlations in the reconstructed environment remain sources of systematic uncertainty.
The data directly reconstruct force ranges only through 8 megaparsecs; extending the limit to longer ranges relies on analytic and numerical arguments that the constraint strengthens with range.
sourceStatus: Full primary preprint read, including data selection, inference, mock tests, systematic variations, and long-range extrapolation. The paper directly supports all material claims; independent corroboration is not yet expected for a newly released preprint.
